say.en: Your trial balance agrees. Does that mean your books are correct? Not always: some errors leave both totals equal. In this lesson: Classify errors as commission, omission, principle and compensating.
Separate errors that affect the trial balance from those that do not.

body.en: *Errors* of commission: wrong amount, wrong account, wrong side, wrong totalling (casting) or carrying forward. Errors of omission: a transaction left out completely or partly. Errors of principle: violating accounting principles, such as treating capital expenditure as revenue expenditure. Compensating errors: two or more errors that cancel each other's effect.

title.en: Which errors does a trial balance catch?

narration.en: The ledger should give ₹50,000 on each side. One-sided errors (partial omission, wrong casting) make the totals differ. Two-sided errors (omission, commission, principle, compensating) leave them equal, so the trial balance cannot reveal them. Before you choose, predict: will an error of principle upset the totals? Which two errors here make the totals differ?
narration.kn: ಖಾತೆಪುಸ್ತಕ ಪ್ರತಿ ಬದಿ ₹50,000 ಕೊಡಬೇಕು. ಏಕಪಕ್ಷೀಯ ತಪ್ಪುಗಳು (ಭಾಗಶಃ ಲೋಪ, ತಪ್ಪು ಕೂಡಿಕೆ) ಮೊತ್ತಗಳನ್ನು ಬೇರೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ. ದ್ವಿಪಕ್ಷೀಯ ತಪ್ಪುಗಳು (ಲೋಪ, ಆಯೋಗ, ತತ್ವ, ಪರಿಹಾರಕ) ಸಮವಾಗಿಯೇ ಬಿಡುತ್ತವೆ, ತಾಳೆ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಅವನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸದು. ಆರಿಸುವ ಮೊದಲು ಊಹಿಸಿ: ತತ್ವದ ತಪ್ಪು ಮೊತ್ತಗಳನ್ನು ಬದಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆಯೇ? ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾವ ಎರಡು ತಪ್ಪುಗಳು ಮೊತ್ತ ಬೇರೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ?

title.en: On the board: Kinds of errors

say.en: Errors are of four kinds. Errors of commission: wrong amount, account, side or casting.
Omission: left out fully or partly. Principle: capital treated as revenue. Compensating: errors that cancel.
Test four errors. Computer debited to purchases: principle, two-sided, the trial balance still agrees.
Sales book undercast: one-sided, the credit side is short. Credit purchase not recorded: omission, still agrees.
Cash paid to Ramesh debited to Suresh: wrong account, right side, still agrees. Agreement is not proof of accuracy.

explanation.en: Wrong amounts, accounts or totals are errors of commission; a transaction left out is an error of omission; capital and revenue mixed up is an error of principle; two errors that cancel each other are compensating.

title.en: Does the error affect the trial balance?

body.en: One-sided errors affect only one account (for example, undercasting the sales book or posting to the wrong side), so the *trial balance* disagrees. Two-sided errors affect two accounts equally (complete omission, error of principle, posting to a wrong account of the right side), so the trial balance still agrees. That is why agreement is not conclusive proof of accuracy.

problem.en: Classify each error and say whether it affects the trial balance: (i) Purchase of a computer ₹30,000 debited to the purchases account; (ii) Sales book undercast by ₹500; (iii) A credit purchase from Latha ₹2,000 not recorded at all; (iv) Cash paid to Ramesh ₹900 debited to Suresh's account.

steps.en: (i) Error of principle (capital item treated as goods): two-sided, no effect on the trial balance.
(ii) Error of commission (casting): one-sided, the credit side is ₹500 short, so the trial balance disagrees.
(iii) Error of complete omission: both sides missing, so the trial balance still agrees.
(iv) Error of commission (wrong account): debit side is still correct in total, so no effect on the trial balance.

answer.en: Only error (ii) makes the trial balance disagree.

i Error of principle (capital item treated as goods): two-sided, no effect on the trial balance.
ii Error of commission casting: one-sided, the credit side is 500 rupees short, so the trial balance disagrees.
iii Error of complete omission: both sides missing, so the trial balance still agrees.
iv Error of commission wrong account: debit side is still correct in total, so no effect on the trial balance.
So the answer is Only error ii makes the trial balance disagree.

heading.en: Remember the four error families: C-O-P-C

body.en: Commission (wrong amount, side, account or total), Omission (left out), Principle (capital vs revenue mix-up), Compensating (cancel out). Ask: "Did both sides change by the same amount?" If yes, the trial balance still agrees.
